chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from Abbad ibn Yaqoub al-Rawajini, from Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I was with Musa ibn Abd Allah in Yanbu, and my travel expenses had run out during one of the journeys. So one of the sons of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Who do you hope for (to intercede) for what has befallen you?' I said, 'Musa ibn Abd Allah.' He said, 'Then your need will not be fulfilled, and your seeking will not be accomplished.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Because I have found in some of the books of my forefathers (peace be upon him) that Allah (Exalted and Majestic) says...' and he mentioned something similar. I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)! Dictate it to me.' So he dictated it to me. I said, 'No, by Allah! I will not ask him for a need after it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of delegating matters to Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the nuanced Shia understanding of *tawakkul* by linking reliance on the Imam to specific divine promises recorded in their inherited books. The companion’s hesitation suggests that true success in delegating matters to Allah requires aligning one's supplication with the precise spiritual authority and scriptural evidence endorsed by the Ahl al-Bayt, rather than mere general trust. This underscores the Imam's role as the living interpreter of Quranic verses, ensuring that reliance is not just emotional but rooted in revealed truth.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from one of our companions, from Abbad Bin Yaqoub Al Rawwajiny, from Saeed Bin Abdul Rahman who said,

‘I was with Musa Bin Abdullah at Yanbu, and my expense monies had depleted in one of the journeys. So one of the sons of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said to me, ‘Who will take care of what has befallen you?’ So I said, ‘Musa Bin Abdullah’. So he said, ‘Then your need would not be fulfilled. Then your seeking would not be accomplished’. I said, ‘And why is that so?’ He said, ‘Because I have found in one of the Books of my forefathers<sup>asws</sup> that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying . . .’, and he mentioned similar to it (the above Hadeeth). So I said, ‘O son of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Dictate it to me’. So he dictated it to me. So I said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I will not ask him for a need after it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from certain individuals of our people from ‘Abbad ibn Ya’qub al-Rawijni from Sa’id ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has said the following:

“I was at Yanbu’ with Musa ibn ‘Abd Allah. My supplies for my expenses were exhausted during certain journeys. A certain person of the children of al-Husayn asked me, ‘Whose assistence do you hope will help out overcome your difficult conditions?’ I said, ‘Musa ibn ‘Abd Allah will provide for my expenses.’ He then said, ‘He, therefore, will not provide you any help, and you will not succeed in your quest.’ I then asked, ‘Why it will be as such?’ He said, ‘It is because I have found in certain books of my ancestors that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “. . . He mentioned a Hadith similar to the previous Hadith.’’” I then said, ‘O descendent of the Messenger of Allah, dictate it to me.’ He dictated it to me and I said, ‘I swear by Allah that I will not ask him (Musa ibn ‘Abd Allah) to help me.’”
